Middle East.headline: One person was killed and one person was injured after a drone attack in Sulaymaniyah
Middle East.body: One person was killed and one person was injured after a drone attack in Sulaymaniyah According to Kurdpress, news sources announced today Wednesday that a car caught fire and exploded in the city of Sulaymaniyah, Kurdistan Region. Sirvan Sarhad, the governor of Dukan city, said that the car exploded at 7:40 in the evening after a fire, as a result of which one person was killed and another person was seriously injured. Middle East.headline: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited
Middle East.body: More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September. The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government.

Middle East.headline: ‘Season of fear’: Escalating Israeli attacks on West Bank olive farmers, deadly strikes...
Middle East.body: ‘Season of fear’: Escalating Israeli attacks on West Bank olive farmers, deadly strikes on Gaza Israeli attacks on war-torn Gaza over the weekend killed at least six Palestinians, including children, despite a year-old ceasefire agreement. Meanwhile, in the occupied West Bank, settler violence continued through the ongoing olive harvest, with UN independent experts on Monday urging Israel to protect Palestinian farmers. Key points - West Bank: Five Palestinians were killed and over 240 injured by Israeli forces or settlers over the past two weeks, with 200 olive harvest-related attacks documented since the start of September - Gaza: Israeli attacks have continued to cause deaths and injuries

Middle East.headline: Famine fears as aid cuts and shipment restrictions coincide in Gaza
Middle East.body: Deir el-Balah, Gaza Strip — Manal Abu Rabie, a displaced mother of six from Beit Lahiya in northern Gaza, received news that the World Food Programme (WFP) was cutting food assistance to the enclave with fear about what is to follow in the coming days. Gaza has suffered from severe shortages of key staples such as eggs, flour and onions after Israel closed border crossings into the enclave on Wednesday. The prices of food and other essentials have skyrocketed, and families who can afford to do so have been bulk buying, in anticipation of a prolonged blockade.

Americas.headline: Haiti — Gang Violence Escalates as UN Security Council Briefed on Mass Casualties
Americas.body: According to a United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti report presented to the UN Security Council, gang violence caused 1,123 deaths and 440 injuries between July and early October. Armed groups are expanding attacks into rural areas, with 689 women and girls raped in July and August, 87 percent of which occurred during gang rapes. In a separate incident, a search is under way for four Salvadoran aviation technicians missing after armed gangs ambushed their vehicle using firearms and explosive devices.

Americas.headline: Colombia — Fatalities Reported in Illegal Gold Mine Collapse
Americas.body: Fourteen people were killed and seven others injured following the collapse of an illegal gold mine in Colombia. The disaster occurred amid ongoing concerns surrounding informal gold mining across the country. Authorities confirmed the casualty figures following the structural failure, with seven individuals receiving medical treatment for injuries sustained during the collapse.

Americas.headline: Colombia — Earthquake Survivors Await Delayed Reconstruction Aid
Americas.body: Ten weeks after a major earthquake struck western Colombia, thousands of affected families remain without promised government aid to rebuild homes and restore livelihoods. Displaced residents in the hardest-hit areas are relying on relatives, neighbors, or limited personal resources to survive. Frustration is growing over delays in concrete support from the administration's Miracle Fund, established to coordinate reconstruction and mobilize public and private resources.

Americas.headline: Canada — Deadly Fire Spreads Rapidly at Military Base
Americas.body: A fast-moving fire at a military base in Canada killed four men and injured dozens of others. Accounts indicate the blaze spread with extreme speed, advancing one kilometer within 30 to 60 seconds before emergency services could contain it.

Africa.headline: Sudan — Escalating drone strikes cause widespread civilian casualties
Africa.body: Recent drone attacks across Sudan have killed over 160 people, according to medics and rights groups. A strike in al-Dibab, West Kordofan state, killed 80 commuters near a transport hub, while attacks in Khartoum killed three children. Additionally, South Sudanese officials reported that a Sudanese military drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region killed approximately 73 people. The escalating strikes threaten regional stability and heighten protection risks for civilians across multiple regions.

Africa.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola epidemic expands as cross-border cases increase
Africa.body: An ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has infected nearly 10,000 people and killed over 4,500 since May. Centered in North Kivu, the virus has spread across eight provinces and spilled across borders, with Kenya confirming eight cases. Humanitarian organizations warn the epidemic will persist without additional aid. Neighboring countries, including South Africa, are tightening border health screenings, while the combined burden of conflict and disease severely restricts children's access to education.

Africa.headline: Somalia — Intensifying US air strikes drive civilian casualties and displacement
Africa.body: An acceleration of United States air strikes targeting armed groups in Somalia is driving civilian casualties and displacement. Affected families report fatalities, injuries, and forced movement as military operations intensify. The surge in air strikes exacerbates existing protection concerns and increases humanitarian needs for impacted communities across the country.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Russian Strikes Target Kyiv Energy Grid amid Intelligence Friction
Europe.body: Russian forces launched missile strikes targeting Ukraine’s energy and civilian infrastructure, hitting power plants in Kyiv. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Kyiv received no advance warning of the attack from partner countries, including the United States, which had previously shared intelligence. Ukrainian Air Force spokespersons confirmed power plants were struck late in the evening without prior notification. The attacks heighten protection and humanitarian concerns regarding winter energy access, while Ukrainian leadership accused Western partners of withholding intelligence and delaying weapons deliveries.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Drone Strike on Park Causes Civilian Fatalities in Nova Vodolaha
Europe.body: A Russian Shahed drone strike hit a public park in Nova Vodolaha, Ukraine, killing six people, including children. The strike highlights persistent risks to civilians and public spaces in populated areas from ongoing aerial attacks.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Military Conducts First Drone Air Evacuation of Injured Soldier
Europe.body: Ukraine’s military reported conducting the first battlefield air evacuation of an injured soldier using a drone. According to military officials, ground rescue was impossible due to surrounding landmines and hostile drones, prompting the aerial extraction.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Afghanistan — UN Warns of Worsening Food Insecurity and Record Child Malnutrition
Asia-Pacific.body: The United Nations and global food security monitors warn that nearly 19.2 million people in Afghanistan, representing 38 percent of the population, are projected to face acute food insecurity between November 2026 and April 2027. Currently, 15.9 million people experience acute hunger, including 3.4 million in emergency conditions. Furthermore, 4.04 million children under five are projected to require acute malnutrition treatment in 2027, with severe acute malnutrition cases expected to reach nearly 1.1 million. Reduced humanitarian funding, high food and transport costs, and limited employment opportunities are driving the deterioration despite a strong agricultural harvest.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar — Junta Defense Minister Defends Airstrikes on Civilian Areas
Asia-Pacific.body: Myanmar's newly appointed regime Defense Minister, Lieutenant General Yar Pyae, publicly defended ongoing military airstrikes against civilian targets, asserting that the bombing operations are intended to achieve peace. The statement came during an address marking the anniversary of the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement, despite intense international and domestic condemnation over severe human rights abuses, civilian casualties, and humanitarian impacts resulting from the military junta's ongoing aerial bombardment campaigns.

Asia-Pacific.headline: India — Second Global Case of Recombinant Mpox Virus Identified
Asia-Pacific.body: Researchers from the Indian Council of Medical Research have detected a travel-associated mpox case in India featuring a rare recombinant virus merging clades Ib and IIb. The finding, published in Nature Microbiology, marks only the second documented inter-clade recombinant monkeypox virus globally, following a similar case identified in the United Kingdom. Health researchers highlighted that the emergence of convergent recombinant strains underscores the critical need for sustained genomic surveillance to monitor viral evolution.
verified_figures: Second documented inter-clade recombinant monkeypox virus globally

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Central & East Africa — Regional Ebola Outbreak and Impacts
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: An ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has expanded to eight provinces, including North Ubangi, while Kenya confirmed its eighth case, raising concerns over cross-border transmission and regional health system strain. To support diagnostic capacity, the World Health Organization granted emergency use listing for a panel capable of detecting the Bundibugyo strain within an hour. Meanwhile, Africa CDC called for improved financial accounting from aid groups for response funds, as health experts warned that compounding conflicts and disease outbreaks in the DRC and Sudan are severely disrupting access to education for an entire generation.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Spain — Severe Flooding from Storm Adam
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Extreme rainfall from Storm Adam caused widespread flooding across eastern Spain, particularly in the Valencia and Alicante regions. The storm resulted in at least four reported deaths and forced the evacuation of over 2,000 residents as swollen rivers submerged communities, swept away vehicles, and severed transportation networks. Emergency response teams, including military personnel, police, and firefighters, deployed helicopters to rescue residents trapped on rooftops.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Coral Sea — Offshore Magnitude 6.4 Earthquake
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the Coral Sea in the southwestern Pacific Ocean at a depth of 23 kilometers. According to the National Centre for Seismology, no casualties or major structural damages were reported following the seismic event.
